text:
alex_devrel: Heads up — supporting customers on Windows 3.9/3.11 having intermittent SSL handshake failures when using our async sample app inside venvs behind a corporate HTTP proxy. Error shows up only in CI or user machines that have strict MITM proxies.

alex_devrel: Example error users paste: 
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:XXXX)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx.RemoteProtocolError: external connection aborted during handshake
```

priya_py: Do they run with HTTPX's trust_env enabled? On Windows if trust_env is true and the proxy injects a cert, sometimes the venv's ssl module fails to load the system store.

alex_devrel: trust_env is default true for our httpx client. Repro steps I used: create venv with python -m venv .venv, pip install -r samples/requirements.txt, set HTTPS_PROXY to corp proxy, run samples/async_generate.py. Repro on Windows 10 with Python 3.9.12 and 3.11.4.

dave_sdk: I saw this pattern before. Two separate axes: (1) Windows venv/OpenSSL/Python build not wired to system CA, (2) our retries hide the original cert error and surface as a generic connection failure.

priya_py: Workarounds that helped internal users: install certifi + patch with certifi-win32 OR set SSL_CERT_FILE env to certifi.where(). Example: 
```powershell
python -m pip install certifi certifi-win32
$env:SSL_CERT_FILE = (python -c "import certifi;print(certifi.where())")
# restart process/terminal
```

rachel_sec: Note: certifi-win32 is convenient but may not be allowed by infosec in some customers. We should list both approaches in docs and call out corporate policy tradeoffs.

alex_devrel: Another oddity: users using pipx or virtualenv (third-party) sometimes get different behavior than venv created by the official installer. Might be due to how the embedded OpenSSL is packaged.

priya_py: For the SDK side I propose: (A) expose a verify/ca_bundle parameter on both sync and async clients (match requests semantics), (B) honor SSL_CERT_FILE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE envs early, (C) expose trust_env toggle, and (D) when cert verification fails, raise a dedicated CertVerificationError with the original cause and a short troubleshooting hint string.

alex_devrel: +1. Also add a short one-liner in error: "Hint: try installing certifi or set SSL_CERT_FILE to your CA bundle" so support can triage faster. The generic "Max retries exceeded" makes debugging impossible.

priya_py: Typing note: we've seen import errors on Python 3.8 in our async helpers because we used typing.Protocol and ParamSpec without typing_extensions. We should add typing_extensions to extras or install_requires for py<3.10.

rachel_sec: From a security doc perspective, include a checklist for Private deployments: how to mount CA bundles, configure proxy allowlist for KMS endpoints, and allow outbound OCSP/CRL checks. Also show how to run openssl s_client to validate the chain.

alex_devrel: sample snippet to reproduce (async + httpx):
```python
# samples/async_generate.py
import asyncio
import httpx
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=\"x\", timeout=10, httpx_client_options={\"trust_env\": True}) as c:
        await c.generate.create(\"say hi\")

asyncio.run(main())
```

dave_sdk: Implementation notes I sketched: when building transport, do: 
```
cafile = os.environ.get('SSL_CERT_FILE') or os.environ.get('REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE') or certifi.where()
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=cafile)
transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(verify=ssl_ctx)
```
Also add explicit exception chaining so our CertVerificationError contains the original SSLError.

priya_py: And in setup.cfg or pyproject, add conditional dependency: 
```
extras_require = {\"py<3.10\": [\"typing_extensions\"]}
```

ci-bot: created issue #4523: add ca_bundle param + trust_env + typing_extensions for older pythons. Link: https://internal/issues/4523

alex_devrel: I'll draft a tiny doc snippet for "Windows devbox troubleshooting" covering certifi, certifi-win32, SSL_CERT_FILE, and how to check OpenSSL version (python -c 'import ssl;print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)'). Will add to samples README and support KB.

rachel_sec: Also recommend adding an FAQ entry: "Why does my async client fail behind a corporate proxy on Windows?" with step-by-step mitigations and notes on corporate policy.

dave_sdk: I'll open a PR to add the verify/ca_bundle param to AsyncClient and sync client, wire SSL context creation, and improve retry logging so the original exception is visible. Will include unit tests mocking certifi to simulate missing CA.

alex_devrel: thanks all — for triage I'll paste the workaround and request logs (openssl s_client and python ssl version). If customers want a quick workaround we can recommend running samples inside WSL where system CA handling is more predictable.

priya_py: good call. WSL tends to avoid Windows-specific venv/OpenSSL packaging issues.

alex_devrel: closing for now, will follow up with PR link and doc changes.
